text:
Brandon Montour waited until the very end. With 33 seconds left in a 4-4 game, the SEA defenseman let go a slap shot that beat Sergei Bobrovsky, and Seattle walked off with a 5-4 win. Montour was a second-round pick of the Ducks in 2014 who went through San Diego in the AHL before the NHL, and on a night when the Kraken needed someone to settle it, he did.

Our numbers say the result was fair but narrow. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count, gave SEA 2.36 to TOR's 2.08, and the simulated replays of every shot had Seattle winning 55 percent of the time. The second period decided it: SEA out-chanced TOR 1.27 to 0.30 and scored three times, including a power-play goal from Chandler Stephenson on a chance worth only 3 percent. Toronto had the better third, 0.96 to 0.23, and Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews scored to tie it, Matthews with 1:30 left. Toronto's power play was sharper too, with two goals from Gavin McKenna on three chances against Seattle's one on five.

The facts don't give us records or streaks for either club, so we can only say what the night showed. Seattle held on through a late push and took the points. Toronto got a three-point game from McKenna and a late rally, but it was Bobrovsky who allowed 2.6 more goals than the chances against him deserved, and that swing was enough to leave the Leafs empty-handed.
